body.p: Ebuilds are sourced and executed by bash, in an environment that the package manager controls. This section describes the properties of that environment which ebuilds may rely on.
Ebuilds and eclasses may use the features of the bash version that their EAPI guarantees:
body.important: Do not use features of a newer bash version than the EAPI allows, even if the bash installed on your system supports them. Doing so will break on systems with an older bash. Note also that the package manager sets bash's compatibility level to the version listed above, so behaviour that has changed between bash versions will follow the older version.

body.p: For characters in the ASCII range, case modification and collation order (LC_CTYPE and LC_COLLATE) are guaranteed to behave as in the C locale. Ebuilds can therefore rely on bash constructs like ${var^^} or on the sorting order of glob expansion, without having to set these variables themselves.
body.note: This guarantee covers the ebuild environment only. External commands that generate output which the ebuild parses may still be affected by the user's locale.

body.p: The failglob option of bash is set in the global scope of ebuilds. As a consequence, a pattern that matches no file results in an error when the ebuild is being sourced, instead of being silently left as a literal string.

body.note: failglob is only set while the ebuild is being sourced, i.e. in global scope. It does not apply inside phase functions.
